religione: religiō, -ōnis (f.) — sacred obligation, rite, scruple, awe (abl. sg.)
rerumque: rēs, reī (f.) — thing, matter; pl. affairs, fortunes, power (gen. pl.) + -que 'and'
resolvit: resolvō, -ere, -solvī, -solūtum — to loosen, untie, undo, unbind (3rd sg. pres.; also 3rd sg. perf.)
revisit: revīsō, -ere, revīsī — to visit again, return to (3rd sg. pres.)
sacer: sacer, sacra, sacrum — sacred, holy, consecrated (m. nom. sg.)
sacrasse: sacrō, -āre — to consecrate, dedicate (+ dat.) (perf. inf., syncopated = sacrāvisse)
sacrum: sacer, sacra, sacrum — sacred, holy (n. acc. sg.) · also m. acc. sg. (sacrum Polyphoetēn)
saeva: saevus, -a, -um — fierce, savage, cruel (n. acc. pl.) · also f. abl. sg. (Gorgone saevā); n. nom./acc. pl. · also f. nom. sg. (dea saeva)
se: suī (reflexive pron.) — himself, herself, itself, themselves (acc.; also abl. sē)
sed: sed (conj.) — but; sed enim, but indeed
sequuntur: sequor, sequī, secūtus sum — to follow (3rd pl. pres., deponent)
sera: sērus, -a, -um — late, tardy (f. nom. sg.; n. nom./acc. pl.) · also f. abl. sg. (sera nocte)
serena: serēnus, -a, -um — clear, cloudless, calm (f. abl. sg.; also f. nom. sg.; n. nom./acc. pl.)
sese: sē, sēsē — emphatic reflexive, himself, itself, themselves (acc.)
signum: signum, -ī (n.) — sign, token, standard (acc. sg.) · also nom. sg. (tessera signum, the watchword)
sin: sin (conj.) — but if, if on the other hand
sola: sōlus, -a, -um — alone, only (f. nom. sg.; n. nom./acc. pl.)
solio: solium, -ī (n.) — throne, seat of state (abl. sg.)
spes: spēs, speī (f.) — hope, expectation (nom. sg.; also acc. pl.)
stant: stō, stāre, stetī, statum — to stand, stand firm (3rd pl. pres.)
sub: sub (prep.) — + abl. under, beneath; + acc. up to, under
subito: subitō (adv.) — suddenly; also subitus, -a, -um, sudden (abl./dat. sg.)
succedunt: succēdō, -ere, -cessī, -cessum — to go up to, advance upon, approach (3rd pl. pres.)
suo: suus, -a, -um — his/her/their own (reflexive poss.) (m./n. abl. sg.)
superi: superus, -a, -um — above, upper; superī (m. pl.), the gods above (gen. sg. m.; nom. pl. m.) · also m. voc. pl. (Superī, address to the gods)
supremo: suprēmus, -a, -um — last, final (m. abl. sg.; also n.)
talia: tālis, -e — such, of such a kind; tālia, such things, such words (n. acc./nom. pl.)
tam: tam (adv.) — so, so much, to such a degree
tartara: Tartarus, -ī (m.); pl. Tartara, -ōrum (n.) — the underworld, the nether depths (acc./nom. pl.)
tendebat: tendō, -ere, tetendī, tentum — to stretch; direct one's course, hasten (3rd sg. impf.)
tendunt: tendō, tendere, tetendī, tentum — to stretch, strain; to head for, make toward (3rd pl. pres.)
tenebant: teneō, -ēre, tenuī, tentum — to hold, keep, occupy (3rd pl. impf.)
teneo: teneō, -ēre, tenuī, tentum — to hold, keep, grasp, detain (1st sg. pres.)
thybri: Thybris, -is (m.) — the Tiber, river and river-god of Latium (voc. sg., Thybrī; also dat. sg.)
tollit: tollō, tollere, sustulī, sublātum — to lift, raise (3rd sg. pres.)
totidem: totidem (indecl. adj.) — just as many, the same number
totum: tōtus, -a, -um — whole, entire (m. acc. sg.; n. nom./acc. sg.)
tris: trēs, tria — three (m./f. acc. pl., = trēs)
tristi: tristis, -e — sad, grim, bitter, harsh (m./f./n. abl. sg.; also dat. sg.)
troiae: Trōia, -ae (f.) — Troy (gen. sg.) · also dat. sg., for Troy (sīc fāta ferēbant)
troiana: Trōiānus, -a, -um — Trojan, of Troy (f. nom. sg.; n. nom./acc. pl.)
tum: tum (adv.) — then, at that time; next
turne: Turnus, -ī (m.) — Turnus, king of the Rutulians, rival of Aeneas for Lavinia (voc. sg.)
tuta: tūtus, -a, -um — safe, sheltered (n. nom./acc. pl.; f. nom./abl. sg.)
tyrrhena: Tyrrhēnus, -a, -um — Tyrrhenian, Etruscan (f. abl. sg.; also n. nom./acc. pl.)
undique: undique (adv.) — from all sides, on every side
unguibus: unguis, -is (m.) — nail, claw, talon (abl. pl.; also dat. pl.)
unum: ūnus, -a, -um — one, a single, the same (n. nom./acc. sg.; m. acc. sg.)
venit: veniō, venīre, vēnī — to come (3rd sg. perf. vēnit, or pres. venit)
ventura: veniō, -īre, vēnī, ventum — to come; ventūrus, about to come; ventūra (n. pl.), things to come (fut. part., n. acc. pl.) · also f. nom. sg. (progeniēs … ventūra)
venus: Venus, Veneris (f.) — Venus, goddess of love, mother of Aeneas (nom. sg.)
vero: vērō (adv.) — in truth, indeed, but; tum vērō, then indeed
vestra: vester, vestra, vestrum — your (pl.) (f. nom. sg.; n. nom./acc. pl.)
veteres: vetus, veteris — old, ancient, long-standing (m./f. nom./acc. pl.)
vident: videō, -ēre, vīdī, vīsum — to see, behold (3rd pl. pres.)
videri: videō, -ēre, vīdī, vīsum — to see; pass. to be seen, seem (pres. pass. inf.)
virum: vir, virī (m.) — man, hero (acc. sg.; also gen. pl., old form = virōrum)
visa: videō, vidēre, vīdī, vīsum — to see (perf. pass. part., f. nom. sg.; n. nom./acc. pl.)
vivo: vīvus, -a, -um — living, lively, quick (m. abl. sg.) · vīvō, -ere, vixī, victum — to live, be alive (1st sg. pres.)
volgata: volgō (vulgō), -āre, -āvī, -ātum — to spread abroad, make common (perf. pass. part., n. nom. pl.)
vos: tū, vōs — you (2nd pers. pl. pron.) (nom./acc. pl.) · also voc. pl. (vōs, aetērnī ignēs)
vota: vōtum, -ī (n.) — vow, promise to a god, prayer (acc./nom. pl.)
